perspective:
Available to Christian Mensah:

- Christian and Jonathan are childhood friends; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian felt anxious and suspicious because Jonathan had been acting differently and seemed to be hiding something important. He arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- Christian heard Jonathan admit that he had been keeping something from him and that he was in some trouble.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered his help and support, telling Jonathan they could face it together.
- Jonathan told Christian the situation was complicated, that he did not want to drag Christian into it, and that he needed support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian began to suspect the trouble might be related to criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it involved anything illegal.
- Jonathan told Christian he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he had not done anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly to make sure Jonathan was safe. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s own investigation led him to believe Jonathan was being framed. He told Jonathan this and said he had leads, then planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Jonathan asked who would do such a thing and thanked Christian.
- Christian came to believe the person behind it was someone close to both him and Jonathan. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it and that it was someone they both knew and trusted.
- Christian decided to confront that person and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person was dangerous but said he trusted Christian to do what was right.
